packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 16 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of work or author. I
opened only PROMPT.md and the image files of this packet. Beyond plain viewing I
made rotated / enlarged working copies of image-002, -003, -005 and -009 in a
private scratch directory (no content added) because part of the text is upside
down or sideways in the supplied images. No web, search, catalogue or edition used. When saving my responses, a
directory listing of the responses folder showed me the file names of other
packets' responses; I did not open any of them.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview, face 1, with ruler): a composite binding remnant. A long
  grey paper/board spine strip carries, on the right, two small parchment
  pieces: (a) upper right, a narrow strip with 3-4 lines of text UPSIDE DOWN
  relative to the image; (b) lower right, a nearly square piece (c. 5 x 5 cm by
  the ruler) with 10 upright lines of text, blank upper margin, a fold along
  the right edge with three sewing/stain holes. At the top, a folded piece with
  an embroidered (thread-wrapped) edge, blank on this side. Traces of an offset
  or pasted script are visible on the grey strip (left of piece b), sideways.
- image-002 = tile of (a); image-003 = tile of (b).
- image-004 (overview, face 2): the reverse. Mostly white paper lining. The
  reverse of (b) (left) shows only faint show-through of c. 9 lines and a small
  red initial/paraph at lower left; reverse of (a) faint show-through; the top
  folded piece shows 6-7 lines of a larger, heavier script, badly rubbed.
- image-005 = tile of that top piece (face 2).
- image-006 / image-007: a separate small folded fragment (c. 5.5 x 3 cm) with
  embroidered lower edge; 7 lines, upright, with red rubrics and red initials.
- image-008 / image-009: the same small fragment from another side, text
  UPSIDE DOWN in the image; a second, larger-script layer is exposed where the
  upper layer is torn; a white paper tab is attached.
- image-010 / image-011: the same small object from the back: blank skin,
  twisted thread, a small flap with red and black letters, nothing connected.
- Single column on every piece; no running titles. Rubrics in red, 2-line red
  initial "A" in (b), red 1-line initials elsewhere, one red underline in (a).
  No interlinear or marginal glosses seen. Script of (a), (b) and the small
  fragment: small formal book hand, apparently one size; the top piece and the
  under-layer of the small fragment are in a larger hand (tentative: a
  different manuscript reused together).
- Tentative interpretation only: short chant/prayer items separated by rubrics
  of the type "Ad vj", "Sabbato collecta". No inference about work or date.

SELECTED SPANS
1. Piece (b), all 10 lines (image-003).
2. Small fragment, 7 lines (image-007; cross-checked on image-009 rotated).
3. Strip (a), 4 lines (image-002 rotated 180 degrees).
Unread: top piece face 2 (image-005), reverse of (b), larger-script under-layer
in image-009, offset traces on the grey strip, flap in image-010/011.

SPAN 1 - image-003 (lines counted from top of the written area in that image;
left edge of text is at the fold, right edge slightly cropped by the turn-in)
image-003 L1: leamus(?) p(er) do(minum?) [red:] Ad vj [red initial Q]uare ieiu
image-003 L2: nauim(us) et no(n) aspexisti hu(m)iliauim(us) a(n)i(m)as
image-003 L3: n(ost)ras et nescisti [red:] Ad v(?) [red initial T]u(n)c i(n)uocab[is?]
image-003 L4: et d(omi)n(u)s exaudiet clamabis (et) dicet
image-003 L5: ecce assum [red:] Sabbato collecta a'(?)
image-003 L6: [2-line red initial A]Desto d(omi)ne supplicac(i)o(n)ib(us) n(ost)ris
image-003 L7: (et) p(re)sta ut hoc solle(m)pne ieiuni
image-003 L8: um q(uo)d a(n)i(m)is corporib(us)q(ue) cura(n)dis
image-003 L9: salubriter institutu(m) est deuoto
image-003 L10: seruitio celebremus p(er) [red:] Do(mi)n[...] (cropped at fold)
Notes: L1 first word begins at the edge; "leamus"/"lcamus", the start of the word
is on the lost preceding line. L3 the rubric after "nescisti" reads "Ad" plus
one or two minims, then a red capital. L5 the red rubric ends in a small "a" with
a suspension stroke. L1-L10 also visible, reduced, on image-001.

SPAN 2 - image-007 (small fragment; top line cut through by the tear)
image-007 L1: [upper halves lost] ...rtare(?) ce...s morum(?) meni...(?)  (not securely read)
image-007 L2: [red:] Ad vj(?) [..] [red initial P]ueri hebreor(um) uestim[enta]
image-007 L3: [..]ta(?) p(ro)sterneba(n)t i(n) uia (et) clamaba(n)t
image-007 L4: [..]ce(n)tes oza(n)na filio dauid b(e)n(e)d(i)c(tu)s q(ui) ue[..]
image-007 L5: [.] no(m)i(n)e d(omi)ni [red sign, R- or V-like] [red initial O?]e(?) ore v(er)b[.](?) [..] [red:] V(?)sa(?)[...]
image-007 L6: [..]litude(?) [red:] Ad ix(?) [red initial O?] [...]urru(n)t(?) turb[.]  (partly under a lifted flake)
image-007 L7: [.]lorib(us) (et) palmis r(e)de(m)ptori obuia(m)
below L7: tops of one more line under the embroidered edge, [illegible].
Notes: the same lines appear upside down on image-009 (overlap, not new text);
there L6 end reads "...ut turb" and L7 "...ib(us) (et) palmis r(e)de(m)ptori obuia".
In image-009 the area above these two lines is a different, larger script on
an exposed second layer (4-5 lines, black with two red initials/rubrics, one
red word in mid-line); I could not read connected words there: [illegible].

SPAN 3 - image-002, strip (a), read with the image turned 180 degrees; line
numbers counted from the top of the strip in that turned orientation
image-002(rot) L1: [lower parts only] ... d(?)e p(?)... et t(?)... [illegible]
image-002(rot) L2: xp(ist)i(?) uoce(?) tonat (et) nubula(?) [word rubbed, illegible]
image-002(rot) L3: [red cross-like sign][red initial P]rincipes [erasure or rubbed gap, c. 4 letters] ..ci(?) (et) Regib(us)(?)   [red line under the right half of this line]
image-002(rot) L4: [small superscript letters, illegible] bere(?) laua(?)... dona(?) i(n) pasch[.](?)
Notes: L3 "Principes" is clear; what follows the gap is uncertain. L4 is
written slightly smaller/tighter and I do not trust any word in it except the
letter shapes given. Blank parchment below L4 (margin).

image-005 (top piece, face 2): 6-7 lines of the larger script running
horizontally, blurred by a tissue/skin layer, plus 2-3 lines of smaller script
running vertically along the right edge; one red mark. No word securely read:
[illegible]. This tile is low in contrast; a raking-light or higher-contrast
image would be needed.

LIMITATIONS
- All pieces are binding waste, cropped on every side; no full line length is
  certain except possibly piece (b), whose lines read continuously.
- Order and original relationship of the pieces is unknown; two hands/sizes are
  present.
- Reverse sides and the larger-script layers remain unread.
- Suggested further views: the reverse of (b) under transmitted light; the top
  piece (image-005) at higher contrast; the small fragment opened flat.
